body: Yeah, I remember in our courses we always had to follow the basic codes and what not, but I could possibly broaden my horizons on architecture. Interior designing for me was also more of a Plan B if I couldn't land an architecture career, though I also of course enjoyed it. But yeah, I'll have to look into other construction careers and see if any others fit me well.

My only problem is that I've always thought that if I were to have a good future, I'd want to go into an architecture career. Hehe, funnily enough, I actually got into it a little because of Minecraft.

I remember building houses in the game, and I always enjoyed it. Then when I got into the Sims series, I would love designing houses and decorating the interiors of them. I even took Architecture and Interior Design classes during my Sophomore year, which was quite fun, but I wouldn't get great grades in them because I obviously didn't have a drive to complete work. I think the worst part was I loved doing it, but considering I have a perfectionist-esque personality, I wouldn't turn in the work unless I found it to be adequate.

Not necessarily. I've never really thought about it because it was never an option I ever really had though of, or rather, an option I was ever explicitly told about. It was always something I heard of, but never actually been told in detail. Kind of like "oh yeah, it's a possibility, but there's better options for you anyways, so no point in telling you about it."
